properties.title: S2-HWM: Sparse Event-Structured Hierarchical World Model for Long-Horizon Surgical Robot Manipulation

properties.version_basis: PDF identified by SHA-256 against assignments.json; title page read.

properties.description: Sparse event-structured hierarchical world model for long-horizon simulated surgical manipulation.
RSSM with a sparse context model, an Event Transition Model, a manager that selects latent goals at event-gated update points and a primitive-step worker, trained by imagination.

properties.algorithm: RSSM with sparse context and event transition model for hierarchical control

properties.population: simulated dVRK-compatible PegTransfer task in SurRoL

properties.description: Repeated transfer stress test, 3 seeds, 50 episodes each
Repeated transfer with induced drop, 3 seeds, 50 episodes each
Closed-loop simulated PegTransfer success for baselines, ablations and stress tests

legacy_cells.FX: Complete extracted PDF, pages 1–8: title and abstract (p. 1); introduction and related work (pp. 1–3); methods including hierarchical policy, sparse context dynamics, Event Transition Model, and manager bootstrap (pp. 3–4); experimental setup, results, ablations, Table 1, and Figure 5 analysis (pp. 4–6); Table 2/Figure 6 and conclusion/limitations (p. 6); references (pp. 7–8). | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: Prefilled A:I were left untouched. The paper evaluates one SurRoL-based simulated PegTransfer task family; the conclusion says broader surgical tasks and physical robotic systems are future work. Extracted Table 2 row/column alignment is disrupted, so no values rely on it. Capability is L4 based on world-model-supported policy learning with reported control results; this is not evidence of clinical deployment or causal treatment identification. Evidence QA: 10/35 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (28.6%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 33 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 2 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: All 8 physical PDF pages were read as extracted text; pages 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 (Figures 1-6 and Tables 1-2) were visually inspected via rendered PNGs.
Table 1 and Table 2 values were verified from rendered images; Figure 5 normalized error curves have no tabulated numeric values.
The legacy row was read from the root workbook (read only). Saved API drafts for B087 were not opened.
Evidence is simulation-only (SurRoL PegTransfer, 3 seeds, high ablation variance) and does not establish physical robot or clinical capability.
Schema validity and quote occurrence do not establish semantic correctness. No independent human review.
notes: S2-HWM adds sparse event evidence, an Event Transition Model and a manager-worker policy to a Dreamer-style RSSM for simulated PegTransfer in SurRoL. Success is 98.7 percent against 76.0 percent for the flat GASDreamerV3 baseline (3 seeds, 50 episodes each), with 91.3 and 88.0 percent on repeated transfer and perturbation. Ablations without the hierarchy, event gating or ETM lose 7 to 31 points with very large seed variance. Classified L4, core, R1 (simulation). Source points: simulation only, no one-step prediction evaluation, no code statement, flat baseline from the authors' retraining.
